title: A Touch Is Not a Fusion

scenes.tts: Is your nervous system built of separate cells, like liver or skin? Or is it one continuous network of fused fibres?
scenes.visual: Title card: A Touch Is Not a Fusion. Two fine branches drift toward each other and meet.
scenes.narration: Is your nervous system built of separate cells, like liver or skin? Or is it one continuous network of fused fibres?

scenes.tts: There were two answers. The neuron theory said each nerve cell is a separate cell, bounded by its own membrane.
scenes.visual: Split screen, left panel: two cells, each outlined by its own membrane, touching at one point. Label: neuron theory.
scenes.narration: There were two answers. The neuron theory said each nerve cell is a separate cell, bounded by its own membrane.

scenes.tts: The reticular theory said the fine branches fuse into one continuous net.
scenes.visual: Right panel: the same branches fused into one net. A single outer membrane runs around the whole net; inside each fused bridge the cytoplasm is continuous, with no membrane across it. Label: reticular theory.
scenes.narration: The reticular theory said the fine branches fuse into one continuous net.

scenes.tts: It comes down to the point where two branches meet. Does one membrane run on, or do two face each other across a gap?
scenes.visual: Both panels zoom to the contact. Close-up one: two branches joined by an open cytoplasmic bridge, the outer membrane running around both, no membrane across the bridge. Close-up two: two separately enclosed branches, their membranes facing across a gap.
scenes.narration: It comes down to the point where two branches meet. Does one membrane run on, or do two face each other across a gap?

scenes.tts: Here is the one idea to carry through. A touch is not a fusion.
scenes.visual: On screen: A touch is not a fusion.
scenes.narration: Here is the one idea to carry through. A touch is not a fusion.

scenes.tts: Whether two touching branches are one cell or two depends on the membrane where they meet. Settling it takes evidence that bears directly on that membrane: seeing it, or testing what crosses it.
scenes.visual: The membrane at the contact glows. Text below: decided at the membrane. Settle it by imaging the membrane, or by testing what crosses it.
scenes.narration: Whether two touching branches are one cell or two depends on the membrane where they meet. Settling it takes evidence that bears directly on that membrane: seeing it, or testing what crosses it.

scenes.tts: Under the best light microscope, two points closer than about two hundred nanometers blur into one.
scenes.caption: Under the best light microscope, two points closer than about 200 nanometres blur into one.
scenes.visual: A soft blur disk spreads over the contact. On screen: light microscope limit, about 200 nm.
scenes.narration: Under the best light microscope, two points closer than about 200 nanometres blur into one.

scenes.tts: The gap at a chemical synapse is about twenty nanometers. That is about ten times below the limit.
scenes.caption: The gap at a chemical synapse is about 20 nanometres. That is about ten times below the limit.
scenes.visual: Drawn to scale: the 20 nm cleft is a thin sliver inside the 200 nm blur disk. On screen: cleft about 20 nm; blur about 200 nm; about ten times. Note: measured only in the 1950s.
scenes.narration: The gap at a chemical synapse is about 20 nanometres. That is about ten times below the limit.

scenes.tts: Depth is worse. Two branches close together, one above the other, can look like one line as you focus through.
scenes.caption: Depth is worse. Two branches close together, one above the other, can look like one line as you focus through.
scenes.visual: Side view of a thick section: two branches stacked close together in depth. As the focal plane sweeps down, their images overlap into what looks like one line. On screen: depth limit roughly 0.5 to 1 micrometre, depending on the optics; section 100 micrometres or more.
scenes.narration: Depth is worse. Two branches close together, one above the other, can look like one line as you focus through.

scenes.tts: Picture one contact under the best light microscope of the eighteen nineties. What does each theory predict you will see?
scenes.caption: Picture one contact under the best light microscope of the 1890s. What does each theory predict you will see?
scenes.visual: Predict card: Under each theory, what does the light microscope show at this contact? Two empty frames: neuron theory, reticular theory.
scenes.narration: Picture one contact under the best light microscope of the 1890s. What does each theory predict you will see?

scenes.tts: The same thing. Two facing membranes and a fused junction give the same smudge.
scenes.visual: Both frames fill with an identical blurred smudge. On screen: one contact cannot decide it.
scenes.narration: The same thing. Two facing membranes and a fused junction give the same smudge.

scenes.tts: So the evidence had to come from elsewhere: from whole cells, from embryos, and from the direction signals travel.
scenes.visual: Three icons appear in turn: a whole stained cell, an embryo, an arrow along a chain of cells.
scenes.narration: So the evidence had to come from elsewhere: from whole cells, from embryos, and from the direction signals travel.

scenes.tts: The answer, for the vertebrate nervous system, is separate cells. They pass signals across specialized contacts, called synapses.
scenes.visual: Return to the split screen; the neuron-theory panel is highlighted. Label at the contact: synapse.
scenes.narration: The answer, for the vertebrate nervous system, is separate cells. They pass signals across specialized contacts, called synapses.

scenes.tts: That is why this matters for development. In vertebrates, development has to wire separate cells to the right partners.
scenes.visual: Several separate cells send out branches toward partner cells.
scenes.narration: That is why this matters for development. In vertebrates, development has to wire separate cells to the right partners.

scenes.tts: A touch is not a fusion. The difference lies at the membrane.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: A touch is not a fusion. The difference lies at the membrane.
scenes.narration: A touch is not a fusion. The difference lies at the membrane.
